drhp.business: Historically engaged in manufacturing cotton yarn, denim fabrics, shirtings, and garments, the Company discontinued its core manufacturing operations due to court-ordered closure of polluting industries in Ahmedabad. It diversified into cotton trading from November 2022 and, after a change in management and control in July 2025, restructured its business to operate solely in the highway construction segment from the quarter ended December 2025.
drhp.expansion: The Company historically manufactured cotton yarn, denim fabrics, shirtings, and garments but discontinued core manufacturing operations following court-ordered closure of polluting industries in Ahmedabad. To ensure business continuity, it diversified into cotton trading from November 2022. litigation.note: The Company's manufacturing unit at Ahmedabad was closed as per the Order of the Supreme Court following the order of the High Court, Gujarat, regarding closure of polluting industries in and around Ahmedabad.

drhp.one_liner: Soma Textiles & Industries Limited has transitioned from a closed textile manufacturing operation into a pure-play highway construction company following a change in management and control.

plants.role: Former textile manufacturing unit (closed per Supreme Court order)

risks.note: The Company has abruptly shifted from textile trading to infrastructure, exposing it to unfamiliar project execution, cost overruns, and capability gaps.
risks.risk: Execution and operational risks from transition into a new line of business (highway construction)

risks.note: Infrastructure is capital-intensive with long payment cycles; cost escalations in materials and project delays can strain liquidity and profitability.
risks.risk: High working capital requirements and cost overruns in infrastructure projects

risks.note: Revenue and growth are tied to related-party contracts; any change in group strategy or financial health could disrupt operations.
risks.risk: Dependence on Holding Company/group entities for project pipeline and business support

risks.note: The sector has low entry barriers for small projects and established players for large ones, pressuring margins and win rates for a new entrant.
risks.risk: Intense competition in the infrastructure and construction industry

risks.note: Input-cost volatility can erode fixed-price contract margins, especially for a company without long-term supplier agreements or scale.
risks.risk: Fluctuation in prices of key construction materials (steel, cement, bitumen, fuel)

risks.note: Changes in government spending, approval delays, or environmental clearances can stall projects and impair revenue recognition.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risks affecting the infrastructure sector

sk.overview: India ranks as the 6th largest exporter of textiles and apparel globally, with the sector (including handicrafts) accounting for 8.21% of the country's total exports in 2023-24 and a 3.91% share of global textile and apparel trade (elsewhere cited as 4.6% of global trade and a 4.5% share ranking fifth in production). The USA and the European Union are the primary export destinations, together making up approximately 47% of India's textile and apparel exports.
